correctness.rationale: The Bessel identity gives an exact canceled score. Positive power-series coefficient comparison bounds the score and light-load density by an integrable dominating function, implying Fisher limit 2/mu^2. As I2/I1=1-3/(2z)+O(z^-2), the residual relative to (sqrt(mu/lambda)-1)Y is uniformly bounded at near-critical load. Exact busy-period moments E[Y]=1/(mu-lambda), E[Y^2]=2mu/(mu-lambda)^3 give I=1/(2mu(mu-lambda))+O_mu(1), with cross and residual terms O_mu(1). Substitution in prior K formulas gives all announced constants and ratio limits. All 275 packaged numerical checks executed successfully; they do not certify the infinite limit.

value.rationale: The first public source explicitly poses analytic behavior at both natural load boundaries as an open problem. The result derives distinct leading exponents and constants and a ratio that diverges at zero load but tends to one at critical load, yielding a concrete surveillance-regime crossover. A critical Bessel-score remainder bound plus exact busy-period second moment is the structural mechanism; the result is not merely tabulation or finite numeric evaluation.
